_comment: MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers the CLIENT may expose as tools.
Copy this file to mcp_servers.json and edit it - mcp_servers.json is seeded from
this template at startup if missing and is NEVER overwritten.
NOTHING IS ENABLED BY DEFAULT. An MCP server is an external process or a remote
endpoint the AI can drive, so 'enabled' is a human decision made in this file (or in
Settings > MCP), and the first use still asks a consent card (stdio -> subprocess
consent, http -> url consent). An http endpoint additionally passes the SSRF gate:
a loopback / LAN / metadata address is refused until you approve that exact URL.
Entry fields:
name        tool-name namespace: tools appear as mcp__<name>__<tool>. Letters/digits/_/.-
enabled     false = never started, never in the schema.
transport   'stdio' (command + args on this machine) or 'http' (url).
command/args  program + arguments for stdio.
env         extra environment variables (merged over the process env).
cwd         working directory for the server process (optional).
url         endpoint for http transport (http:// or https:// only).
headers     extra request headers for http, as an object. A value may be "${NAME}":
the secret then lives in the environment and only the reference is stored
here; an unset variable means the server does not connect and says which
one. '${NAME}' reads the CLIENT PROCESS environment (not this entry's
'env', which is only passed to a stdio child). Names are case-insensitive,
values printable ASCII on one line, max 16 headers. Host/Content-Type/
Accept/Mcp-Session-Id are set by the transport.
roles       which CLIENT roles may use this server. '*' = any. An unknown role adds nothing.
timeout_sec per-request wall clock (default 30, clamped 1..300).
